name: funeral rites

attributes.attribute: carved on stones marking some graves
practiced at the graves of rulers
feet bound to stop the dead from stray

sources: MacCulloch, J. A. The Religion of the Ancient Celts. London: Constable, 1911.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ancient Celtic funeral rites followed burial rather than cremation or burial. Burial was the usual practice. Stones bearing Ogham characters may have stood above some graves. The stones were not reserved for people of lower status. Grave goods were common in Celtic graves. People placed chariots, coins, ornaments, and weapons with the dead. The items were meant to accompany the dead to the Otherworld. Signs hint that rulers' graves once hosted human sacrifice. Skulls come away from the other bones, a mark of decapitation. Both archaeology and the old records show the living feared that the dead might come back. Some rites tried to stop the dead from wandering. Mourners bound the feet of corpses to keep them in place. Later customs left the feet free. The change helped the dead reach the Otherworld and stopped them from troubling the living.

okr.objective: The entry describes ancient Celtic funeral rites and grave customs.
key_results: Celtic peoples used burial rather than cremation.
grave-goods included chariots, coins, ornaments, and weapons.
Some rites bound the feet to stop the dead from roaming.
